holdout_discrepancy_analysis.root_cause: run_h1.py defines get_holdout_examples(derived, val_unanswerable_count=20) which returns val_unanswerable_sorted[20:]. The F1 protocol defined the holdout as val_unanswerable_sorted[28:] (after the 20 train + 8 val experiment pool). The H1 code does not use the 20 derived unanswerable in training (H20 replaces them), so it repurposes the split at index 20 for the holdout boundary.
holdout_discrepancy_analysis.protocol_split: indices 0-19 = experiment_pool (20 train + 8 val), indices 20-41 = holdout (14 actual)
holdout_discrepancy_analysis.actual_split: indices 0-7 = validation (8), indices 8-19 = UNUSED (12), indices 20-41 = holdout (22)
holdout_discrepancy_analysis.effect_on_benchmark: NONE — benchmark evaluation uses 182 frozen examples and is independent of holdout split
holdout_discrepancy_analysis.effect_on_h1_conclusions: LOW — the holdout is a secondary diagnostic. H1 abstention on 22 holdout (36.4%) is directionally consistent with the 14-example holdout subset (which would be the last 14 of the 22)
